note_text: Properly stored cooked rice lasts 3–6 days in the refrigerator, not 24 hours. The key safety rule is to refrigerate it within 2 hours of cooking to prevent bacterial growth like Bacillus cereus. [URL] https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/does-rice-go-bad
search_results:
**The claim that cooked rice must be thrown out after 24 hours is incorrect.** Food safety guidelines and expert sources recommend refrigerating cooked rice within 2 hours of cooking and storing it in an airtight container in the fridge for **3–6 days**, depending on the type of rice and storage conditions[1][2][3][4].

### Key Supporting Facts from Sources
- Refrigerate cooked rice within **2 hours** to prevent bacterial growth like *Bacillus cereus*, but it remains safe for much longer than 24 hours when properly stored[1][4]. (https://www.riceland.com/the-riceland-blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-storing-and-reheating-rice-tips-tricks-from-riceland-foods)
- Cooked rice (white or brown) lasts **4–6 days** in the fridge in an airtight container[1][2]. (https://www.riceland.com/the-riceland-blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-storing-and-reheating-rice-tips-tricks-from-riceland-foods, https://www.chicorice.com/blogs/all-about-rice/how-to-store-brown-rice)
- General consensus: **3–5 days** at 40°F (4°C) or below[3], or **3–4 days** (up to a week per some sources) before quality or safety declines[4]. (https://reencle.co/blogs/news/blogs-news-blog-safe-rice-storage-and-spoilage-guide, https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/does-rice-go-bad)

No sources support discarding after exactly 24 hours; the 24-hour idea likely confuses the "danger zone" rule (food out >2 hours) with total fridge shelf life. Freezing extends usability to 6–8 months[1][2][4]. Check for spoilage signs like off smells, mold, or sliminess before eating[4].
